This demo is based on the Jaeger HotROD demo but has 
been modified considerably to showcase Signadot & Sandboxes.

![image](/docs/graph.png)


## Running

First, [install Signadot Operator](https://www.signadot.com/docs/installation/signadot-operator)
if you haven't already.
Next, install and configure the [Signadot CLI](https://www.signadot.com/docs/getting-started/installation/signadot-cli).

### Install the HotROD Application

Decide on a namespace in which to install HotROD and then run:

```bash
kubectl create ns "${NAMESPACE}"
kubectl -n "${NAMESPACE}" apply -k k8s/overlays/prod/<devmesh | istio>
```

To uninstall:

```bash
kubectl delete ns "${NAMESPACE}"
```

workload. Be sure to replace `<cluster-name>` and `<namespace>` with the
appropriate values for your setup:

content.text:
The fare estimate and ride history work end to end across the driver, location and frontend services, and the UI shows both.

I tested it with the real stack in a browser: MariaDB, Redis and Kafka in Docker, all four services running, and a few rides requested through the UI. I also added Go unit tests for the fare math, the ride-history validation and the proxy; `go build` and `go test ./services/...` pass. I couldn't run the repo's Playwright or Cypress suites here, because the runner isn't installed. Instead I checked in the browser that their selectors and the Cypress regex still match the new notification body.

## What changed

**Driver**
- The fare is $1.50 per minute of ETA, with a $3.50 minimum, rounded to the cent. The code is in `services/driver/fare.go`.
- The notification body is now `Driver T748384C arriving in 10m44s. Fare: $16.10`. The existing ETA and plate parsing still work on it.

**Location**
- There is a new `ride_history` table: pickup name, dropoff name, request time, driver plate and fare.
- `GET /ride-history` returns `{rides, total}`, newest first, with an optional `limit` (default 50).
- `POST /ride-history` creates an entry and returns 201.
- `PATCH /ride-history` takes an id plus driver plate and/or fare, and returns the updated entry.
- Bad input gets a 400, and an unknown id on PATCH gets a 404.
- The table is created at startup with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, and again on demand if it goes missing. I did not reuse the existing lazy `setupDB`: it would try to re-seed `locations` and panic on any database that already has data, which is every existing deployment. I tested exactly that case.

**Frontend**
- The three endpoints are proxied to the location service through the traced client, so routing and baggage headers carry over. The location service's status and body are passed through unchanged.
- The ETA countdown now shows the fare, for example "…will arrive in 10:42 · Fare $16.10".
- A new "Ride History" card sits below the ride form, with a table of pickup, dropoff, time, plate and fare, plus a "Total rides" badge.
- After a dispatch succeeds, an entry is created. When the driver notification arrives with plate and fare, the entry is updated by PATCH and the table refreshes.
- I rebuilt `web_assets` the same way `build.sh` does, so the old hashed JS file was replaced by a new one.

## Existing bug I fixed
The countdown restarted from the full ETA on every page re-render. For example, picking a location jumped it from 03:01 back to 03:57. It only happened on re-renders and the new history refreshes would have triggered it more often, so I made the target time stable per request. After the fix the countdown keeps ticking when I change a dropdown.

## Notes
- To run the driver locally I had to set `SIGNADOT_BASELINE_*` and run a throwaway fake routes server, because the driver blocks until a routes server reports "synced". That setup was temporary and is already removed. Nothing in the repo depends on it.
- The console errors in the browser come from the map's external OSRM service, which isn't reachable from this sandbox. The favicon 404 was already there.
- I stopped and removed the Docker containers and temporary binaries I started.

## Existing bug I fixed
The countdown restarted from the full ETA on every page re-render. For example, picking a location jumped it from 03:01 back to 03:57. It only happened on re-renders and the new history refreshes would have triggered it more often, so I made the target time stable per request. After the fix the countdown keeps ticking when I change a dropdown.
